name: Georgia
headline: Georgia: +7.5% growth in 2025, 3.9% inflation, debt 34% of GDP
sections: Georgia is a $38.1 billion economy (2025), the world's 109th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +7.5% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $29K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 8.0% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 3.9% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 11.9% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 13.9% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 30.3% (2025).
Gross government debt is 34% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 60% in 2020. The general government balance is −1.5% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −2.6% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 101% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 4.3% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 32% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 74.7 years (2024). Population: 3.9 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
